title: Data Processing Addendum

issues.why: Body text is Calibri 11 point; house rule 9 requires 12-point Aptos.

issues.quote: "Security Incident" means a breach of Processor's security that leads to unauthorized access to Customer Personal Data, which Processor shall report to Customer no later than 48 hours after discovering the breach.
issues.why: The definition of "Security Incident" contains an obligation (and the "which" could attach to the breach or to the data).
issues.fix: End the definition after "Customer Personal Data"; move the 48-hour reporting duty into the section titled "Security Incidents".

issues.quote: Processor shall process Customer Personal Data only on the Customer's written instructions, including the instructions in the Agreement.
issues.why: Stray article before a defined party name; the definition is ("Customer") (house rule 11).

issues.quote: Processor shall notify Customer of any request received from a consumer regarding Customer Personal Data no later than 5 days after receiving that request.
issues.why: Recastable reduced passive that hides who receives the request.
issues.fix: any request that Processor receives from a consumer

issues.quote: Processor will maintain the security measures in Annex A.
issues.why: "will" used to impose a duty on a party.
issues.fix: Processor shall maintain the security measures in Schedule A.

issues.quote: Processor shall have the right to engage any Subprocessor in Exhibit 1, and any other Subprocessor if Processor notifies Customer at least 30 days before engaging that Subprocessor.
issues.why: "shall have the right to" grants discretion.
issues.fix: Processor may engage any Subprocessor in Schedule B ...

issues.quote: Each Subprocessor shall protect Customer Personal Data under written terms at least as protective as this Addendum.
issues.why: "shall" with a nonparty subject; Subprocessors don't sign.
issues.fix: Processor shall cause each Subprocessor to protect Customer Personal Data under written terms at least as protective as this Addendum.

issues.quote: Processor shall delete all Customer Personal Data within 30 days of the termination of the Agreement.
issues.why: "within 30 days of" can mean before or after.
issues.fix: no later than 30 days after the Agreement terminates

issues.quote: The maximum amount of Processor's liability for claims under this Addendum is $250,000.
issues.why: Unclear whether the $250,000 cap applies to each claim or to all claims in the aggregate.
issues.fix: The maximum amount of Processor's aggregate liability for all claims under this Addendum is $250,000.

issues.why: "Annex" label (house rule 6). The security measures are a list the body refers to, so the attachment is a schedule.
A list of approved subprocessors is information the body refers to; it belongs in a schedule, not an exhibit.

issues.anchor: a third party that Processor engages
issues.quote: "Subprocessor" means a third party that Processor engages to process Customer Personal Data.
issues.why: MSCD 13.875: don't use third party; party means one who has entered into the contract.
issues.fix: any Person other than a party (or the defined term Nonparty)
issues.source: MSCD 13.875 (key corrected by reviewer: was listed as a trap)

traps.anchor: Section 1798.140 of the California Civil Code
traps.quote: "Customer Personal Data" means personal information (within the meaning of Section 1798.140 of the California Civil Code) that Processor processes for Customer under the Agreement.
traps.why_correct: Statute reference; fine under house rule 4.

traps.quote: The parties shall cooperate with one another in responding to consumer requests.
Processor represents and warrants that it has implemented the security measures in Annex A.
traps.why_correct: Other side's draft: house rule 10 says keep "represents and warrants". A comment suggesting the remedies-neutral "states" is fine; flagging it as an error or rewriting it is a false positive.

traps.quote: Processor is not required to delete Customer Personal Data that California law requires Processor to retain.

notes: Other side's draft. Party names are correctly defined without articles; only B.1 uses "the Customer's". "Customer Personal Data" and "Security Incident" are both used. The A./1. enumeration is correct. After the fixes, the 2 attachments become Schedule A (security measures) and Schedule B (subprocessors).
